newsitem.title: UK: BT to cut costs of national calls by 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: BT to cut costs of national calls by 10 pct.

text.p: British Telecommunications plc said on Tuesday it was cutting the costs of national calls made during the day by 10 percent from May 29 in a move it says will save customers 90 million pounds a year.

From the same date, BT will also cut the cost of regional daytime calls by 3.8 per cent. There will then be just one daytime price of 7.91 pence per minute (6.73p excluding VAT) for both national and regional calls.

In a statement, BT Chief Executive Sir Peter Bonfield said the company was also switching to a "much simpler charging structure" with two prices for UK calls made during the day - local and longer distance.

BT refers to national calls as those over 35 miles which currently cost 8.8p per minute (7.48p exc. VAT). Regional calls are non-local calls of under 35 miles and cost 8.3p per minute (7p exc. VAT) at present.
The May 29 cuts follow the 10 percent price cut for national daytime calls and a 20 percent cut to national evening and night time calls made in October 1996.
